Large language models builds on top of [autoregressive](/thoughts/Autoregressive-models) [transformers](/thoughts/Transformers) to predict the [next token](/thoughts/Autoregressive-models#next-token-prediction).

This is often because these models are trained to "hillclimb" this specific objective, and with the recent advancement in [RL](/thoughts/Reinforcement-learning) we've basically achieved _pseudo-intellectualism_

There are also a whole genre of language model built on top of diffusion blocks, where it learns to reconstruct masked tokens, then generates text through repeated unmasking <small>(diffusion is an alternate approach to AR, but if anything it lacks the coherency formed via [superposition](/thoughts/mechanistic-interpretability#superposition-hypothesis) to those of AR models (_i suspect_))</small> (Nie et al., 2025).

[Speculative decoding](/thoughts/Speculative-decoding) techniques such as DFlash uses a lightweight block-diffusion draft model to produce a block of draft tokens in one forward pass for an autoregressive target model to verify (Chen et al., 2026).

> [!note]- GPTs and friends
>
> Most variants of LLMs are decoder-only (Radford et al., 2019). There are bi-directional encoder-decoder models, though their application are more domain-specific, whereas decoder-only models generalized a lot better, per recent history.

Have "capabilities" to understand [natural language](/thoughts/NLP).

Exhibits [emergent behaviour](/thoughts/emergent-behaviour) of [intelligence](/thoughts/intelligence). ^emergent

One way or another is a form of [behaviourism](/thoughts/Behaviourism), through [reinforcement learning](/thoughts/Machine-learning). It is being "told" what is good or bad, and thus act accordingly towards the users. However, this induces [confirmation bias](/thoughts/confirmation-bias) where one aligns and contains his/her prejudices towards the problem.

### Scalability

Incredibly hard to scale, mainly due to their [large](/thoughts/large-models) memory footprint and tokens memory allocation.

### [Optimization](/thoughts/optimization)

- [Quantization](/thoughts/quantization): reduce computational and memory costs of running inference with representing the weight and activations with low-precision data type
- [Continuous batching](/thoughts/Continuous-batching): update the batch after each decoding step so finished requests leave and waiting requests can join. [Orca](https://www.usenix.org/conference/osdi22/presentation/yu) introduced iteration-level scheduling. [PagedAttention](/thoughts/paged-attention) manages KV-cache memory in blocks; it can support this scheduling by reducing wasted memory.
- Different [Attention](/thoughts/Attention) variants, for better kernels and hardware optimisation (Think of [Flash Attention 3](/thoughts/flash-attention), [Radix Attention](/thoughts/radix-attention), [TreeAttention](/thoughts/tree-attention), etc.)
- [Byte-Latent Transformer](/thoughts/Transformers#byte-latent-transformer): group bytes into variable-length patches using next-byte prediction entropy. The large transformer processes patches, while a smaller decoder generates bytes autoregressively. [^blt]

[^blt]: A small byte-level model estimates how uncertain the next byte is. High uncertainty starts a new patch; predictable byte sequences can share longer patches, reducing the number of steps run by the large transformer. Entropy determines patch boundaries. Byte generation still uses the decoder's next-byte predictions. See [BLT, sections 2.3 and 3](https://arxiv.org/html/2412.09871v1).

>
> We do math to internalise the concept, and practice to thinking coherently. Similarly, we [write](/thoughts/writing) to help crystalised our ideas, and in the process improve through the act of putting it down.

The process of rephrasing and arranging sentences poses a challenges for the writer, and in doing so, teach you how to think coherently. Writing essays is an exercise for students to articulate their thoughts, rather than testing the understanding of the materials.

### on [ethics](/thoughts/ethics)

There are ethical concerns with the act of "hallucinating" content, therefore alignment research is crucial to ensure that the model is not producing harmful content.

For [medicare](/thoughts/university/twenty-four-twenty-five/engineer-4a03/finals), ethical implications requires us to develop better [interpretable models](/thoughts/mechanistic-interpretability)
